Play report

I reached level 4 of 6 and did not beat the game. I beat levels 1–3, then the move timer ran out on level 4, which ended the game. The service now refuses further actions, and I did not call `/reset`.

**How the game works:**
- Actions 1–4 move a 4×4 marker up, down, left and right on a board. Its exit is a 9/a-coloured box joined to the board. A move into a wall still uses up time.
- The column at the right edge is a timer that drains as you act, and running out is game over.
- The 3×3 panel at the bottom is set by clicking its cells. When it matches a pattern shown on the left, the matching power fires:
  - **Plus shape:** shrinks the marker to 2×2 so it fits through narrow corridors.
  - **Corner L shape:** teleports the marker to marked spots on a separate board.
  - **Vertical line:** fires a shot in the direction of the last move. Hitting the switch box (colour 6) removes the door (colour d) that blocks the exit.

**What happened on each level:**
- **Level 1:** shrank the marker, went up the narrow corridor to the exit.
- **Level 2:** teleported to the second board and moved into the exit.
- **Level 3:** my first shot went the wrong way, because I hadn't yet learned it follows the last move. I lined up under the switch, moved up and fired, which opened the door, then went down to the exit.
- **Level 4:** I fired at the switch without shrinking first. The 4-wide shot couldn't enter the 2-wide corridor to the switch, so it stopped. I then shrank the marker, but the timer was too low to line up and shoot again. I headed for a pickup in the timer's colour, guessing it would refill the timer. Each move was draining 4 rows by then, and the timer ran out a few moves short of it.

On another attempt, the fix for level 4 is to shrink first, line up with the narrow corridor, then shoot, without wasting the earlier moves. It may also help to grab the timer-coloured pickup early.

The board had an exit on the right, blocked by a door. A switch box stood at the top of a corridor two cells wide, and destroying it opens the door. You destroy it by setting the bottom panel to a vertical line, which fires a shot in the direction of your last move.

I used up a lot of the timer before getting anywhere:
- I made one accidental move as the level began.
- I fired upward with the full-size 4×4 marker. The shot was 4 wide, couldn't enter the 2-wide corridor and stopped. That cost a move plus three clicks.
- Only then did I set the panel to the plus shape, which shrinks the marker to 2×2, and step it under the corridor.
- By that point there were only about 8 moves left. I gambled on reaching a timer-coloured pickup, hoping it would refill the timer, but each move was now draining 4 rows instead of 2, and the timer ran out short of it.

The cause of failure was spending actions on trial and error: the wasted shot and the late shrink.

**2. Can it be beaten?**

I think so. The plan, starting with the 4×4 marker at rows 29–32, columns 37–40 (that is where it was after my stray move, so the true start may be one step higher):
1. Click the four edge cells of the panel to make the plus shape; the marker shrinks to 2×2, keeping its top-left corner.
2. Move left 3 times to column 31, which lines up with the corridor.
3. Move up once, so the last move points up.
4. Click the three centre-column cells to fire; the shot should go up the corridor, destroy the switch and open the door.
5. Move down to the door's rows, then right about 13 times through the doorway to the exit.

That is roughly 25 actions. Things I still need to check:
- Whether the shot will now pass up the narrow corridor. Level 3 suggests it will, once it is aligned.
- The real timer budget. A move cost 2 rows early in the level and 4 rows late; I don't know if clicks, the panel effects, or the marker's size change the cost.
- Whether the shrunk marker steps 2 cells at a time all the way to the exit.
- If the budget is short, whether the timer-coloured pickup really refills it, and how to reach it cheaply.

**3. Next attempt**

I'll make no stray moves, run the plan above exactly, and check the timer after every action. If the rate projects that it will run out before the exit, I'll detour to the pickup early, while there are still enough moves left to do it.

**1. What happened on level 4**

The board has a 4×4 marker, an exit on the right behind a door, and a switch box at the top of a corridor two cells wide. Shooting the switch opens the door. Every action drains a 64-row timer, and the game ends when the timer is empty. A pickup in the bottom-left corner refills part of the timer.

The marker's abilities come from matching a 3×3 panel to patterns shown in a legend:
- the **plus pattern** shrinks the marker to 2×2, or regrows it to 4×4;
- the **vertical line** fires a shot in the direction of the last move.

In my best attempts I did the following:
1. Moved the 4×4 to the bottom left and shrank it.
2. Collected the pickup with the 2×2.
3. Moved to the spot where regrowing lines the 4×4 up with the corridor, and regrew.
4. Shot the switch, which opened the door.
5. Walked toward the exit.

The timer ran out about 3 moves short, three attempts in a row. Early attempts also wasted actions on trial and error: a misaligned shot, picking up the refill too early, and a wrong guess about where the regrown marker lands. The underlying failure is that every route I found costs more than the timer provides.

**2. Can it be beaten?**

I can't tell either way.

What I'm claiming: under the mechanics I've found, the cheapest route costs about 14 rows more than the available budget.

The costs and constraints behind that:
- **Timer costs:** a move or click costs about 3.4–3.6 rows; a completed pattern costs about one action's worth extra.
- **Marker positions:** a 4×4 only stops at columns 21, 25, 29, 33, 37 and 41, and rows 21, 25, 29 and 33. The shot needs the corridor (columns 31–32) under the left half of the marker. So shrinking is unavoidable, and then either a 2×2 shot at column 31 or a regrow to a 4×4 at column 31.
- **Cheapest route without the pickup:** 10 moves, 11 clicks and 3 completed patterns, about 86 rows against 64.
- **With the pickup:** it adds about 36 rows, but only a 2×2 collects it, and reaching it costs at least 8 extra moves. That route is about 114 rows against about 100.
- **Other orderings** cost the same or more.

What it rests on: my measurements over eight attempts, and the assumption that no mechanic remains undiscovered. A designed level suggests one does, perhaps a cheaper action, facing changes that cost nothing, or something in the corridor or switch area. Testing those would settle it.

**3. Rules I worked out, and from what**

- **The shot follows the last move.** On level 3 the first shot went right after a rightward last move; the next went up after an upward move.
- **The shot needs the corridor under the marker's left half.** A 4×4 at columns 29–32 was blocked with the corridor at 31–32. A 2×2 at column 31, and a 4×4 at columns 31–34, both passed.
- **Shrink and regrow anchor differently.** Shrinking kept the top-left corner (rows 25–28, columns 37–40 became rows 25–26, columns 37–38). Regrowing expanded up and to the left (a 2×2 at row 25, column 35 became a 4×4 at row 23, column 33).
- **Only the 2×2 collects the pickup, and the refill adds rows.** A 4×4 covering the pickup gave nothing. The 2×2 took the timer from 30 rows to 62.
- **Shooting the door doesn't open it.**
- **Patterns must match exactly.** Plus shape and centre cell together did nothing.
- **Unmatched clicks persist on the panel.**
- **Clicks on the legend or the board are free.** They only give hints or a red flash.

**4. Rules I'm still unsure about**

- **The exact timer cost and whether it varies.** Decrements alternate between 2 and 4 rows, so my budget arithmetic carries about ±1 action of error.
- **Whether the refill is capped at 64.** I've only collected it below about 28 rows.
- **Whether turning without moving changes the shot direction.** A move into a wall turns the marker but costs as much as a move, and I don't know if the shot then follows the new facing.
- **Whether any cheaper or hidden action exists.** That's the doubt behind leaving the verdict undecided.

VERDICT: undecided
CONFIDENCE: 45
